newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on auction, EMU convergence trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on auction, EMU convergence trade.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed across the board in midday trade on Tuesday in the wake of a successful auction and on the back of positive EMU convergence trades, dealers said.
The National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said on Tuesday that a 150 million Irish pound auction of the eight percent bond due 2006 was covered 5.15 times.
The stock, sold to primary dealers in a competitive auction, achieved an average price of 108.24 to give an annual yield of 6.77 percent, the NTMA said.

"We had the auction which went very well. We saw good demand for the 06's before and during the auction which was taken out very comfortably. The market is in good shape across the board in its aftermath," Padraic Garvey, economist at Riada Stockbrokers, said.
"There has been a convergence theme to trade, which has been positive. This afternoon's CPI data from the U.S. will tell a story in terms of direction," he added.

By 1115 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 25 pence from Monday's close at 101.80 to yield 6.02 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 57 pence from the close at 108.37 to yield 6.75 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 139 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 84 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area.
